description: Give one of question (search), query_id (read a Q_ query's source), path (read by library path), or a library-wide read: list/recursive/intent (the tree, or every query with its intent) or source_matches (search the query sources)

list.description: Show one level of the library as a tree (directories with query counts, and the queries directly in directory, default /) instead of searching. Does not combine with question (use intent to filter a listing)

limit.description: how many results: in a question search the matches (default 8, up to 25); describing a commit the queries shown; in a recursive listing the page size (default 200, up to 1000); in source_matches the matching queries shown (default 100, up to 500). A one-level list ignores it

commit_id.description: read query_id or path at this library commit instead of the head. Refused with recursive or intent (the listing reads the head); with source_matches it sets the commit the sources are read at

recursive.description: with list (or alone): list every query under directory at any depth, each with its intent and id, instead of one level

intent.description: keep only the queries whose @intent text matches this regular expression (Go RE2; case-sensitive unless it starts with (?i); ^\s*$ finds the queries with no intent). Alone or with list/recursive it gives the recursive listing; with question it filters the matches; with source_matches it narrows which sources are read

source_matches.description: search the SOURCE of the organization's saved queries under directory (default /) for this regular expression (Go RE2; a literal dot is \.): lists each query with its first matching lines. At most 300 sources are read per call; a larger set is partial and says so. Does not combine with question, list or recursive

repository.description: ORG keeps only the organization's own queries, FWD only Forward's built-in ones (any case); in a recursive listing, an intent filter or a question search (a one-level list refuses it). source_matches reads only ORG sources, so FWD is refused with it

offset.description: in a recursive listing: rows to skip, to page past the first 200 (limit sets the page size, up to 1000); in source_matches: qualifying queries to skip, moving the window of up to 300 sources read per call. Each result says the offset to continue at. Not with question
